docs.title: Accounts
docs.snippet: On DigitalOcean, you manage your infrastructure and billing with teams. Your personal account on DigitalOcean lets you manage your team membership and your name, sign-in method, and email subscriptions.

docs.title: 29 June 2026

docs.title: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings
docs.snippet: DigitalOcean’s terms of service prohibit accounts registered to addresses from OFAC-sanctioned countries. For more information, including a list of countries, see section 5.7 of our **Rules of Conduct** in our terms of service.

docs.title: Name
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Name
docs.snippet: At the top of the **Profile** tab, the **Name** section displays the name on your account. Click the **Edit** button to change it.

docs.title: Sign-in Method
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method
docs.snippet: The **Sign-in method** section lets you choose how you log in to your DigitalOcean account. You can use:

docs.title: Email Address and Password
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method > Email Address and Password
docs.snippet: If you currently use email and password to sign in, you can choose **Update email address** to change your email address.

docs.title: Google or GitHub Accounts
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method > Google or GitHub Accounts
docs.snippet: If you currently sign in with a Google or GitHub account, the account email address is displayed in the **Sign-in method** section.

docs.title: Email Preferences
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Email Preferences
docs.snippet: The **Email subscriptions** section includes a link to the Subscriptions Preference Center, which lets you opt in or out of the emails you receive from us.

docs.title: Your Teams
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Your Teams
docs.snippet: The **Your teams** section lists any DigitalOcean Teams you are part of. The team **name**, your **role** (member, biller, or owner), **status** (invited or joined), and join date (if applicable) are listed in the table.

docs.title: Deactivate Account
docs.heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Deactivate Account
docs.snippet: How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data: Deactivate an account to stop billing and prohibit future resource creation. Optionally purge your account data to permanently remove the account from DigitalOcean and prevent account reactivation.

docs.title: How to Change the Control Panel Theme
docs.heading_path: How to Change the Control Panel Theme
docs.snippet: The theme controls whether the DigitalOcean Control Panel displays with a light or dark appearance. You can select a theme directly or have the control panel match your operating system’s appearance setting. Your selection is saved as a personal preference.

docs.title: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts
docs.snippet: If you log in to DigitalOcean with a username and password, enabling 2FA adds an additional layer of security against unauthorized access to your account.

docs.title: Learn more about two-factor authentication.
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Learn more about two-factor authentication.
docs.snippet: An *authentication factor* is a piece of information used to verify that you’re allowed to do something, like a keycard used to unlock a hotel door.

docs.title: Default Account Authentication
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Default Account Authentication
docs.snippet: When you first create your account, 2FA is disabled, but DigitalOcean takes other steps to protect your account.

docs.title: Enabling Two-Factor Authentication
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication
docs.snippet: To enable 2FA for your DigitalOcean account, log in to the DigitalOcean Control Panel, in the top right corner, click the profile icon, and then click **My Account** to go to your **My Account** page.

docs.title: Choosing the Second Factor
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Choosing the Second Factor
docs.snippet: Scroll to the **Two-factor authentication** section, and then click **Set Up 2FA**.

docs.title: Using an Authentication App (Recommended)
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Using an Authentication App (Recommended)
docs.snippet: Authenticator apps like Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, Microsoft Authenticator, and Duo are small, free mobile applications used to generate security codes. They work globally and are more secure than SMS because they don’t transmit the security codes across the network.

docs.title: Using SMS
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Using SMS
docs.snippet: If you select SMS, your mobile carrier must be able to deliver a text message, which means you need mobile signal or an internet connection. This may be inconvenient when traveling internationally. In addition, because SMS messages are vulnerable to being intercepted by hackers,…

docs.title: Choosing a Backup Method
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Choosing a Backup Method
docs.snippet: Once you’ve configured your primary method for 2FA, you need to add a backup method. This is how you can regain access to your account if your 2FA device is lost or stolen.

docs.title: Backup Codes (Recommended)
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Backup Codes (Recommended)
docs.snippet: Backup codes act like a second password, so store them in a secure place that you can access without your phone.

docs.title: Authenticator App
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Authenticator App
docs.snippet: You can use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Duo as your backup solution.

docs.title: Disabling Two-Factor Authentication
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Disabling Two-Factor Authentication
docs.snippet: You can disable 2FA on the **My Account** page, in the **Two-factor authentication** section. Click **Disable 2FA** to disable two-factor authentication.

docs.title: Switching Authenticator Apps
docs.heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Switching Authenticator Apps
docs.snippet: If you have enabled 2FA for your account and are using an authentication app, you can change the current app you are using to authenticate your DigitalOcean account by disabling 2FA and then enabling it again using your preferred authentication app.

docs.title: Credit Card

docs.snippet: When you connect a PayPal account, you choose a payment method from PayPal and allow a $5 authorization charge. This verifies the payment method for use on DigitalOcean.

docs.snippet: DigitalOcean has a monthly billing cycle. On the first calendar day of each month, we invoice and charge accounts for the previous month’s resource usage, applying signup credit and taxes when applicable.

docs.snippet: If we cannot collect an outstanding balance, for example, after a monthly charge on the first day of the month fails or after a mid-month charge at your tier’s auto-charge amount fails, the same enforcement process applies.

docs.title: Permanently Deleted Resources
docs.snippet: If an unresolved balance continues after suspension, we may permanently delete the account’s resources. Deleted resources cannot be recovered. The account owner can still pay the balance to access the account, but they must recreate any resources that were removed.

docs.snippet: Each Droplet plan includes an amount of free outbound data transfer. Additional outbound transfer is billed at $0.01 per GiB. Inbound transfer to Droplets is free.

docs.title: Details and Examples
